This box triggers once when the room initializes, and it is the first to trigger

A room initialization happens when someone enters the room after the room has been empty for more than 30 seconds, or when the room is reloaded (:reload command)

It is a highly recommended Wired practice to reset your full game to its "initial" state when this box triggers, as your room may have been "killed" in an unexpected state, such as when a maintenance break happens when players are mid-game

wiredmenu.error_info.title: Wired Error Information
wiredmenu.error_info.0:
This error occurs when the maximum Wired usage limit (which can be observed in the "Monitor" tab) is about to be exceeded by a Wired execution.
When this happens, the execution of Wired will be cancelled, such that the Wired usage limit is never exceeded.

Reaching the execution cap too quickly may be a sign of an inefficient Wired setup.
If your Wired setup is not too complex, you should investigate how to improve the setup to avoid this error from unexpectedly happening. The Wired usage is a great indicator of your room's Wired complexity, and other factors (such as lag in the Habbo servers) are not at play.
wiredmenu.error_info.1:
Delayed Wired events happen when you execute a Wired effect that has a delay configured.
There is a limit to how many of these delayed Wired events can be awaiting execution at the same time, otherwise a smart setup with Wired signals could cause a memory leak in the Habbo servers.

In any normal scenario, it would be rare to receive this error. If for some reason you do, you may have made an error in your Wired setup. If you haven't made an error, you should transform your Wired setup to use Wired counters instead
wiredmenu.error_info.2:
This error occurs when the Wired engine is receiving a lot of instructions, but the Habbo servers can not keep up with it.
This is usually a sign of server issues, and may not necessarily have to do anything with your room.

If your room also gives the "MARKED_AS_HEAVY" warning, your room may be a contributing factor and you could look into making the Wired setup less complex
wiredmenu.error_info.3:
The Habbo servers are analyzing the time it takes to execute your Wired setup at all times, and may consider it to be a "heavy" Wired setup if certain boundaries are exceeded. What happens as a result, is that your room is treated slightly different to avoid it from interfering with other rooms in the hotel. There is no reason to panic as this is not an error, but just a warning. However, you shouldn't completely ignore it too.

What this means for a wired creator is:
- Ignore the message if Habbo is lagging, it may not be related to your wired setup.
- Ignore this message if your room is actually a complex wired room. It's just a notification in that case, so you're aware.
- If none of the above, and it's supposed to be a simple room, then you're doing something wrong and should probably improve the Wired setup.
wiredmenu.error_info.4: This is an error that occurs when the Habbo server suspect your room from having malicious Wired intentions. For that reason, the exact criteria for when this happens will not be disclosed.\n\nThe penalty for this error is that Wired execution is halted for 10 minutes.
wiredmenu.error_info.5:
Recursive wired events happen when signals execute other Wired stacks in the room. It may do that 10, 100, or 1000+ times before actually concluding the Wired execution. If the Habbo servers analyze that this is taking too long, it will stop your Wired execution.

This Wired error rarely occurs, but it sometimes does when there is lag on the Habbo servers and the Wired room is either inefficient or complex.
In most cases, another Wired error will already have stopped your Wired execution before this error can occur.
wiredmenu.error_info.6:
This error occurs when you have given too many different Wired variables to a user or a furni. However, this limit is very high and is not something you should be reaching.
If you are reaching this limit, it may be a sign that you're trying to use variables in a repetitive or wrong way, to achieve a goal variables aren't fit for.

If you are trying to use Variables to store long lists of data for a user or furni, you should be aware that that is not possible and you may require a more creative solution to solve your problem.
If you are familiar with the concept of "bit operations" or are open to learn about it, you can use it to store more data on a single Wired variable (depending on the use case).
Wired variable values are 64-bit signed integer values, and bit operations are located under the advanced math operators.
